environmentalPersistence: Moderate — soil half-life 60–120 days; volatilizes from plant surfaces; persists longer in cold soils

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate — phytotoxic effects on cell membranes reduce growth
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Moderate — contact phytotoxicity causes leaf margin curl and burn
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Moderate — disruption of chloroplast membrane function
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate — contact necrosis at application points; spreads to adjacent tissue
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Moderately inhibited — soil residues affect root tips
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Both affected; contact spray affects sprayed surfaces regardless of age

physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Moderately reduced — organophosphate effects on guard cell metabolism

microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Strongly suppressed — AChE-inhibiting effects on microbial enzyme systems

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: Poor — persistent in tissue; partial recovery on new growth after ~4 weeks

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Discrete necrotic spots at contact points; background chlorosis; mild yellowing
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Contact spray points on leaf surface
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Discrete contact necrosis spots distinguishes chlorpyrifos from systemic herbicides
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate — TCP metabolite and MDA signature
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Strongly reduced; high pathogen fraction; resistome elevated
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Minimal — spots remain; new growth healthier after 4+ weeks

synergies.synergyNote: Organochlorine + organophosphate combination represents the historical progression of pesticide classes — used together they provide overlapping resistance coverage; both disrupt microbiome severely

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Agricultural insecticide on fruits, vegetables, soybeans, corn; residential use banned in US 2001; agricultural use pending EPA review since 2015
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: One of the most widely used agricultural insecticides in the US — ~10 million lbs/year on food crops
educationalContext.humanToxicity: High — acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; causes neurodevelopmental damage in children; IARC Group 2A; linked to autism spectrum disorder and reduced IQ at prenatal exposure levels. Banned in EU, under review in US.
educationalContext.climateLink: Warmer temperatures increase volatilization and atmospheric transport of chlorpyrifos — expanding exposure zones beyond application areas
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Primarily outdoor agricultural; residential use banned
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: On fruits and vegetables in US grocery stores — direct food exposure. The child neurodevelopment story (EPA's own science found harm but reversed the ban under Trump administration then reinstated under Biden) is a textbook example of science-policy interaction.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Children's neurodevelopment, food safety, science-policy interaction, EU vs US regulatory differences

sources: Eskenazi B, et al. (2007). Organophosphate pesticide exposure and neurodevelopment in young Mexican-American children. Environmental Health Perspectives, 115(5), 792–798.
